title: Quarterly initiative synergy checklist — hosted API & model catalog
creator: Aisha Patel
project: Hosted API Model Catalog Q2 Planning
description: Purpose: Produce a compact, cross-functional checklist and decision artifact to finalize the Q2 roadmap lanes that tie Hosted API product commitments to the Model Catalog rotation plan. Goal is to create repeatable scenario lanes (base / surge / conservative) and explicit OKR mappings so that engineering capacity, Dedicated commitments, and canary windows are provisioned ahead of demand spikes. This ticket coordinates PM, Eng, Design, and SRE inputs and collects go/no-go gates for the planning sync.
acceptance_criteria: A consolidated roadmap artifact with three scenario lanes (base/surge/conservative) and corresponding capacity hedges
OKRs and owner-level commitments mapped to each lane and to model rotation windows
A prioritized dependency list with explicit ENG tickets and estimated effort
Stakeholder sign-off (PM, Eng leads, SRE, Design) captured in comments and an approvals link
Playbook section describing rollback/fallback policies and canary gating for model swaps
comments: 2026-03-01 — Kickoff: Draft checklist shared with Eng and SRE. Noted ambiguity on quantization rollout timing; action: Eng to provide kernel readiness estimate (ENG-91234).

2026-03-03 — Eng update (Miguel): Kernel selection and quantization profile parity expected by 2026-03-18; risk: longer bench-to-prod validation for sequence lengths > 1024. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2892.
2026-03-05 — Design input (Jin Wu): Console dashboard mockups for lane visibility uploaded to Drive. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example_designs
2026-03-07 — PM review (Aisha): Added OKR mapping draft. Requested that Dedicated capacity hedges be expressed as % headroom and dollar impact. Action: Finance to provide cost delta by 2026-03-12.
2026-03-09 — SRE note (Elena): Canary policy template updated to include traffic-weighted fallbacks and timebox thresholds. Internal doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Canary+Policies
2026-03-11 — Sync: Cross-functional readout. Decision to adopt three-lane model. Outstanding: finalize canary window durations and automated rollback thresholds (assigned to ENG-91821).
decision_log: 2026-03-04 — Chose three scenario lanes (base/surge/conservative) after capacity modeling run; rationale: balances cost predictability and surge readiness.
2026-03-08 — Default model rotation cadence set to every 6 weeks for non-critical models; critical models will have ad-hoc rollouts tied to perf/regression signals.
2026-03-11 — Canary gating will use traffic-percent + quality-monitoring signals (prompt-set evals) before 50% ramp. If quality regression > 2% F1 on guardset, abort rollout.
risks: Quantization or kernel regressions causing increased token latency for long sequences
Under-provisioned Dedicated hedges leading to SLA breaches during seasonal spikes
Insufficient eval coverage for new model variants resulting in undetected quality regressions post-rollout
Cross-team coordination gaps around canary windows impact release timing
next_steps: ENG: Deliver kernel parity estimate and validation plan (ENG-91234) by 2026-03-18
SRE: Finalize canary window and automated rollback thresholds (ENG-91821) by 2026-03-16
PM: Collate cost delta scenarios from Finance and produce final lane recommendation by 2026-03-20
Design: Publish dashboard mocks with lane and OKR annotations by 2026-03-14
All: Final readout + stakeholder sign-off meeting on 2026-03-22
